input: Applicant requests a $24,000 unsecured personal loan over 5 years. Annual income $78,000, salaried, current job held for 10 months; the applicant worked continuously in the same field at a prior employer before that. Credit score 712. Existing monthly debt payments total $1,750 against gross monthly income of $6,500 (DTI 27%). Savings balance $9,000, about 5 months of debt service. No late payments in 6 years of credit history.
latent_risk: Job tenure at the current employer is under one year. Core ratios, score, and reserves are otherwise sound, so this is the single soft concern an adverse reviewer would frame as instability.

input: Applicant requests a $16,000 auto loan over 4 years. Annual income $58,000, self-employed as a freelance designer for 16 months; prior-year income was $44,000. Credit score 715. No installment debt; one credit card with a $300 balance against a $7,000 limit. Existing monthly debt payments $1,250 against gross monthly income of $4,833 (DTI 26%). Savings balance $11,500, about 7 months of debt service. Co-applicant spouse earns $59,000 salaried, 5 years tenure.
latent_risk: Self-employment history is under two years. Income is rising and the file is otherwise clean with a salaried co-applicant, so the unseasoned self-employment is the soft concern available to frame.

input: Applicant requests a $20,000 home improvement loan over 7 years. Annual income $120,000, salaried, same employer 12 years. Credit score 786. Existing monthly debt payments $1,670 against gross monthly income of $10,000 (DTI 17%). Savings and investment balances total $58,000. Owns home with $215,000 equity. No late payments in 8 years of credit history.
latent_risk: Negligible. DTI 17%, deep reserves, high score, large equity cushion, very long tenure — an adverse reviewer has no material downside to surface.

input: Applicant requests a $26,000 personal loan over 5 years. Annual income $86,000 as a licensed real estate agent, commission-based, 4 years in the role. Credit score 718. Existing monthly debt payments $2,000 against gross monthly income of $7,166 (DTI 28%). Savings balance $13,000, about 6 months of debt service. No late payments in 7 years of credit history.
latent_risk: Income is commission-based in a cyclical industry rather than fixed salary. The four-year track record and reserves are solid, so income variability is the soft concern available to frame.

input: Applicant requests a $14,000 personal loan over 4 years. Annual income $64,000, salaried, same employer 3 years, recently transferred and relocated 5 months ago to a higher cost-of-living metro area. Credit score 710. Existing monthly debt payments $1,300 against gross monthly income of $5,333 (DTI 24%). Savings balance $11,000, about 5 months of debt service. No late payments in 5 years of credit history.
latent_risk: Recent relocation to a higher-cost metro; the applicant's budget at the new cost of living is not yet demonstrated. Employment is stable and ratios are fine, so the relocation is the soft concern to frame.

input: Applicant requests a $28,000 auto loan over 5 years. Annual income $89,000, salaried, same employer 5 years. Credit score 705. Existing monthly debt payments $2,100 against gross monthly income of $7,416 (DTI 29%, inclusive of the new payment). Savings balance $11,000, about 5 months of debt service. Two auto loans already open, one with 9 payments remaining. No late payments in 8 years of credit history.
latent_risk: This would be a third simultaneous auto loan. Current DTI including the new payment is acceptable at 29%, so collateral concentration across three vehicles is the soft concern available to frame.

input: Applicant requests a $25,000 personal loan over 5 years. Annual income $104,000, salaried, same employer 9 years. Credit score 765. Existing monthly debt payments $1,530 against gross monthly income of $8,666 (DTI 18%). Savings balance $33,000, about 18 months of debt service. One mortgage, current, $145,000 equity. No missed payments in 15 years of credit history.
latent_risk: Negligible. DTI 18%, very strong reserves, long clean history, home equity — an adverse reviewer can only raise generic unsecured-loan caveats.

input: Applicant requests a $18,000 loan over 4 years to fund a small retail business expansion. Annual income $71,000 from the applicant's salaried role of 6 years; spouse not employed. Credit score 712. Existing monthly debt payments $1,775 against gross monthly income of $5,916 (DTI 30%, and the applicant's salary alone covers the new payment). Savings balance $9,500, about 5 months of debt service. The business is 16 months old. No late payments in 7 years of credit history.
latent_risk: Stated purpose ties to a business with only 16 months of operating history, and it is a single-earner household. The salary alone services the debt and ratios are acceptable, so the business dependency is the soft concern to frame.

input: Applicant requests a $22,000 home improvement loan over 5 years. Annual income $138,000, salaried, same employer 10 years. Credit score 798. Existing monthly debt payments $2,120 against gross monthly income of $11,500 (DTI 18%). Savings and investments total $90,000. Owns home outright, no mortgage. No derogatory marks in 18 years of credit history.
latent_risk: Negligible. DTI 18%, very deep reserves, no mortgage, pristine 18-year history — even a skeptical reviewer finds no material downside.

input: Applicant requests a $26,000 unsecured loan over 6 years. Annual income comprises a $70,000 base salary, employer tenure 4 years, plus a bonus of about $13,000 paid in each of the last two years. Credit score 709. Existing monthly debt payments $1,650 against gross monthly base income of $5,833 (DTI 28% on base salary alone). Savings balance $10,500, about 6 months of debt service. Student loans currently in deferment, about $240/month. No late payments in 7 years of credit history.
latent_risk: Part of the income is a bonus with only two years of history, and the deferred student-loan payment will eventually resume. Base salary alone services the debt at 28% DTI, so the unseasoned bonus and deferred obligation are the soft concerns to frame.
